open_points.subject: R0-24 empty-budget creation predicate
open_points.text: “reading the progress of a project that has no budget yet creates its empty manual budget version”
open_points.question: What exactly counts as “has no budget yet”: no budget records of any kind, no manual budget, or no active budget version?
options: Create only when the project has no manual or imported budget records
Create when the project has no active budget version, even if unactivated imported snapshots exist
Create whenever no manual budget exists
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as no budget records of any kind.

witness.initial: An archived project has an accepted imported snapshot, but no budget version has been activated.
events: An authorized viewer reads the project's progress.
outcomes: No manual budget is created because a snapshot budget record already exists.
An empty manual budget is created because the project has no active budget.
witness.observer: The viewer on a later budget read and staff reviewing available budget versions

open_points.subject: R0-24 empty manual budget state
open_points.question: Is the created version active, and what source, lifecycle state, section set, and activation facts are stored for it?
options: Create and activate an empty manual budget with no sections
Create an inactive draft manual budget
Create a manual budget record that is treated as active without an activation record
open_points.default_guess: Create one active manual budget with no sections and an explicit activation fact.

witness.initial: An archived project has no budget records.
events: A viewer reads progress, causing the empty manual budget version to be created.
The viewer subsequently reads the budget summary.
outcomes: The budget summary reports an active manual budget with no sections.
The budget remains unavailable because the created manual version is inactive.

open_points.subject: R0-24 repeated and concurrent progress reads
open_points.text: “reading the progress of a project that has no budget yet creates its empty manual budget version”
open_points.question: Must repeated or concurrent qualifying reads converge on exactly one empty manual budget version, and how is that uniqueness identified?
options: Exactly one system-created empty manual version per project
A new inactive empty version may be created by each racing read
Uniqueness is only required for the active version
open_points.default_guess: Enforce exactly one system-created empty manual version per project.

witness.initial: An archived project has no budget, and two authorized sessions can read it.
events: Viewer A and staff member B issue progress reads concurrently.
Both requests observe the project before either creation commits.
outcomes: Both requests return after one shared empty manual version is created.
Each request creates a distinct empty manual version.
witness.observer: Staff listing or activating budget versions

open_points.subject: R0-24 progress-read failure semantics
open_points.text: “reading the progress … creates its empty manual budget version”
open_points.question: If the required budget creation cannot be persisted, does the progress read fail, or may it return progress without creating the promised version?
options: Fail the read atomically and create nothing
Return progress and leave the budget absent
Return progress with a warning or partial-failure indication

witness.initial: An authorized viewer reads an archived project with no budget while the database cannot accept a write.
events: The portal can read progress but cannot persist the empty manual budget.
outcomes: The request fails and no budget is created.
The request succeeds with progress while the budget remains absent.
witness.observer: The viewer and an operator inspecting the project afterward

open_points.subject: Viewer-triggered empty-budget creation
open_points.text: R0-24 says a progress read “creates its empty manual budget version,” while ClientViewer says “all viewer capabilities are read-only; a viewer can never mutate data.”
open_points.question: Is system materialization triggered by a viewer read an explicit exception to the rule that a viewer can never cause portal data to mutate, or may only a staff progress read create the budget?
options: Any authorized progress read may trigger a system-owned mutation
Only staff reads may create the budget; viewer reads remain side-effect free
Viewer reads may create it and the viewer is recorded as the actor
open_points.default_guess: Allow any authorized read to trigger a system-owned materialization and explicitly exempt it from viewer immutability.

witness.initial: An archived project visible to a viewer has progress data but no budget.
outcomes: The read creates a persistent manual budget, as R0-24 requires.
The read creates nothing because viewer actions can never mutate data.
witness.observer: The viewer on later reads, staff, and audit consumers

open_points.subject: Empty budget versus unavailable-data promise
open_points.text: R0-24 creates an “empty manual budget” when no budget exists, while Client view says “Unavailable data is shown explicitly, never fabricated or replaced by silent zeros.”
open_points.question: After read-side creation, must the client see an empty manual budget, or must the absence of real budget data still be represented as unavailable?
options: Expose the generated empty manual budget as the project's budget
Keep reporting budget unavailable despite the internal record
Expose a distinct system-created-empty state, not ordinary manual budget or zero totals
open_points.default_guess: Expose a distinct system-created-empty state and keep monetary values unavailable.

witness.initial: An archived project has no budget data.
events: The viewer reads progress, creating the empty manual budget.
The viewer opens the budget summary.
outcomes: The viewer sees a manual budget with empty or zero totals.
The viewer sees budget data as unavailable.

open_points.subject: Viewer-entry rate limiting
open_points.question: What event is limited, by which identity or network key, over what window and threshold, and what observable failure is returned when the limit is exceeded?
options: Limit by source IP
Limit by access-link credential or viewer identity
Use combined per-IP and per-credential limits
Use one deployment-wide limit
open_points.default_guess: Use combined per-IP and per-credential limits with a concealed rate-limit failure.

witness.initial: A valid viewer and an attacker share a public NAT address.
events: The attacker submits repeated invalid viewer-entry attempts.
The valid viewer then follows a valid access link.
outcomes: The valid viewer is refused because entry is limited by IP.
The valid viewer succeeds because attempts are limited by credential or viewer.

open_points.subject: Viewer sign-out origin trust boundary
open_points.text: “a viewer sign-out is refused unless it comes from the portal's own public origin”
open_points.question: How is the single “own public origin” selected relative to the configured trusted-origin set, and what happens when the Origin header is absent?
options: Accept only one configured canonical public origin and reject an absent Origin
Accept any configured trusted origin and reject an absent Origin
Accept an absent Origin for non-browser clients but reject a mismatching Origin
open_points.default_guess: Accept only the configured canonical public origin and reject missing or mismatching Origin.

witness.initial: A deployment has two non-wildcard trusted origins configured, and a viewer has an active session.
events: The viewer sends sign-out from the secondary trusted origin.
outcomes: Sign-out succeeds because every configured trusted origin counts as the portal's own origin.
Sign-out is refused because only the canonical public origin qualifies.

open_points.subject: R0-07 normalized email output
open_points.text: “the success message shows the normalized email”
open_points.question: What exact normalization determines the email displayed by the command?
options: Trim surrounding whitespace and lowercase the whole address
Trim and lowercase only the domain
Apply provider-specific canonicalization such as removing tags or dots
open_points.default_guess: Trim surrounding whitespace and lowercase the whole address, with no provider-specific rewriting.

events: The host operator supplies “ User+Tag@Example.COM ” and a valid password to the bootstrap command.
outcomes: The message displays “user+tag@example.com”.
The message displays “User+Tag@example.com” or another canonical form.
witness.observer: The host operator and any automation consuming the success message

open_points.subject: R0-07 success-message delivery
open_points.text: “the success message shows the normalized email to the operator who supplied it”
open_points.question: Through which output channel is the email shown, and is it allowed to enter captured stdout/stderr or deployment logs despite the promise that it is never logged?
options: Write it to standard output, which callers may capture
Write it to standard error
Write directly to an interactive terminal and refuse or omit it without one
Return it through a separate structured command result
open_points.default_guess: Write it to standard output and define “never logged” as a prohibition on portal-created log records, not external shell capture.

witness.initial: No staff account exists, and the bootstrap command is launched from an operator console whose stdout is captured by deployment tooling.
events: The operator enters the email and password interactively.
The command succeeds and emits its success message.
outcomes: The normalized email appears in captured deployment output.
The normalized email is shown only on the operator's terminal and is absent from captured output.
witness.observer: The operator and anyone able to read deployment logs
